editorial_thesis: W42 was not a simple model-release week. Frontier agent execution (Wonder, Argon), hyperscaler silicon and active-compute economics (Maia 300, LFM2.5), licensing constraints on open-weight deployment (Muse terms, Apache 2.0, OpenMDW-1.1, Kommunity output-only), software-engineering orchestration (Codex practice, Scion, HydraFusion plus delivery gates), operational safety boundaries (disclosed incidents, distillation defenses, ECDSA closure, evaluator access), and scientific agency (closed-loop wet-lab, geospatial reasoning, review infrastructure) advanced together. The issue reports which system capability is real and what remains merely a vendor claim, keeping usable numbers with denominators and license conditions visible.
architecture_goals: Distinguish vendor-demonstrated agent execution from independently verified long-horizon performance (P1).
Ground inference economics in named silicon mechanisms while marking unnamed-baseline efficiency claims as vendor-only (P2).
Compare open-weight architectures on parameters, active parameters, context, and inference feasibility together with actual license texts and conditions (P3).
Separate coding productivity evidence from maintenance cost, merge-bottleneck, and security-gate realities (P4).
Draw the line between disclosed safety incidents, vendor defense claims, closed methodological mysteries, and unevaluated access mechanisms (P5).
Weigh scientific-agent methods by denominators, artifacts, ablation design, and stated limitations rather than headline scores (P6).
Place domain-specialized and embodied systems on independent anchors while keeping older papers as background, not launches (P7).

page_plan.notes: Sol r8 seven-package design: body subtotal 26.5 pages (P1 4.0, P2 2.5, P3 5.0, P4 4.0, P5 3.0, P6 4.5, P7 3.5) plus 1-2 pages opening/methodology/sources; target ~27-30 pages, not a hard cap.
